why.text: Cool, humid Atlantic summers and southerly winds ripen Hondarrabi grapes slowly. The whites are high in acid, with citrus and herbal notes.

styles.text: Light, lightly acidic whites with citrus and herbal notes; also rosado, red and barrel-fermented white.

climate.text: Atlantic, humid and mild, with cool summers and mostly southerly winds at ripening; wines reach 10.5 to 11.5 % alcohol.

altitude.text: Vineyard land at or below 400 m, anywhere in Bizkaia.

tastes.text: Whites: pale to straw yellow, greenish; white and citrus fruit, herbs; lightly acidic, slightly bitter finish. Rosés: strawberry to raspberry; wild berries. Reds: picota to violet; lightly tannic. Barrel whites add balsamic notes.

styles.name: Txacolí blanco fermentado en barrica
styles.text: White fermented in barrel; white and citrus fruit, herbs, balsamic notes.

why.text: Stony, slate-rich soils on steep slopes regulate rainwater. Cold winters and very hot summers shape the wines.

styles.text: Young and oak-aged reds and whites; fruity, with floral notes and, when aged, spice and toast.

climate.text: Low winter temperatures, very hot summers and a long frost period.

soil.text: Stony soils with abundant slate, on steep slopes.

tastes.text: Reds: ruby to cherry red; fruity and floral; aged reds add balsamic, spice and toast from oak. Whites: pale yellow to greenish; fruity with floral and mineral touches; aged whites are spiced and toasty.

why.text: Vineyards lie mostly by the sea, in a mild Atlantic climate with 1,600 mm of rain. With neutral soils, they give high-acid txakoli.

styles.text: Fresh, light whites with a slight spritz; also rosado, red and barrel-fermented white.

climate.text: Mild Atlantic: about 1,600 mm of rain, mean 18 to 20 °C during ripening, south and southwest winds late in ripening.

soil.text: Neutral soils, with most vineyards close to the sea.

tastes.text: Whites: pale green-yellow to gold; fresh, with fine fizz and a slightly bitter finish. Rosés: pink to fuchsia; citrus, green fruit. Reds: red-garnet; wild berries, light acidity. Barrel-fermented whites: new wood notes.

styles.name: Txakoli blanco fermentado en barrica
styles.text: White fermented in barrel; golden, balanced, new wood notes.

why.text: Slightly acid soil sits under an Atlantic climate with frequent south wind. The txakoli is round and low in acid, with citrus and herbal flavours.

styles.text: Whites, rosados and reds, plus barrel-fermented white; whites show green apple and citrus, with a slight bitter finish.

climate.text: Atlantic; mean 13.1 °C (highs 18.7, lows 7.5) and south wind on about 170 days a year.

tastes.text: Whites: pale yellow to straw; green apple, tropical fruit, citrus; lightly acidic. Rosés: pale to salmon; red fruit; slight fizz. Reds: black cherry, violet tints; slightly bitter finish. Barrel whites: toast and citrus.

styles.name: Txakolis blancos fermentados en barrica
styles.text: White fermented in barrel; toasted barrel notes with citrus fruit.

why.text: Pergola-trained vines grow in a humid Atlantic climate on poor, thin, acidic soils. Albariño dominates the zone and gives acid, aromatic wines.

styles.text: Albariño and other whites, some oak-aged; also red and quality sparkling wine.

climate.text: Atlantic, close to the sea and humid.

soil.text: Low pH, poor in minerals and nutrients, and thin.

tastes.text: Albariño: straw yellow with gold or green tones; citrus, floral and apple aromas; light acidity, good structure. Barrel whites: toast, smoke, vanilla. Reds: picota with violet tones; red fruit; lightly tannic.

styles.name: Rías Baixas Albariño
styles.text: White with great aromatic complexity: citrus, floral and apple.

styles.name: Barrica
styles.text: Barrel white: golden; toast, smoke, vanilla and dried fruit.

styles.name: Vino espumoso de calidad
styles.text: Quality sparkling wine: fine, persistent bubble, fresh and fruity.

why.text: Steep terraces on slate and granite rise above the Miño and Sil canyons. Long, hot summers ripen Mencía and Godello.

styles.text: Reds, whites and rosados, usually young, some aged in barrel; Mencía leads the reds, Godello the whites.

climate.text: More continental than Atlantic: long hot summers, mild autumns, 700 to 800 mm rain, mean 11.3 °C, strong winds.

soil.text: Alluvial soils over slate, with more granite in places.

tastes.text: Reds: cherry to purple red; red berry or stone-fruit aromas; balanced. Whites: pale to golden yellow; white tree fruit. Rosés: pale pink to cherry; wild berries. Barrica wines: spice, wood or oak.

styles.name: Súmmum
styles.text: Made with a higher share of the principal (preferred) grape varieties.

styles.name: Barrica
styles.text: Aged in oak barrels; spice, wood or oak aromas.

styles.name: Guarda
styles.text: Aged in wood barrels or other tanks.

why.text: Sloping, sometimes terraced vineyards sit in a Mediterranean-oceanic climate. Godello comes out structured and Mencía red-fruited.

styles.text: Godello whites and Mencía reds; also quality sparkling wine and Tostado, made from raisined grapes.

climate.text: Mediterranean-oceanic climate; vines grow on slopes, sometimes steep terraces.

tastes.text: Whites: pale yellow, greenish to amber; fresh, fruity, soft, light. Reds: violet-ruby picota; ripe red fruit; fleshy, dry, medium-high acidity. Tostado: intense, floral and honeyed, sweet.

styles.name: Tostado
styles.text: Wine from raisined grapes; floral, honeyed, intense and sweet.

styles.name: Producción controlada
styles.text: Stricter limits on yield per plot.

styles.name: Crianza
styles.text: Aged in wood; wood shapes its character.

styles.name: Gran Reserva
styles.text: Aged longer in wood; wood shapes its character.

why.text: The climate is temperate Atlantic, with big day-night swings and little rain after fruit set. Rugged, thirsty soils give fresh, balanced wines.

styles.text: Fresh whites and reds, plus Tostado, a naturally sweet wine from grapes dried indoors.

climate.text: Temperate Atlantic, with large day-night temperature differences and little rain from fruit set.

soil.text: Rugged, harsh soils with low water-holding capacity.

tastes.text: Whites: pale to golden yellow; ripe and fresh fruit, flowers, honey, herbs; fresh, light. Reds: violet to cherry red; fruit, flowers, spice; fresh, medium to high tannin. Tostado: amber to mahogany, sweet.

styles.name: Ribeiro Tostado
styles.text: Wine from raisined grapes; amber to mahogany, honeyed, sweet and long.

why.text: Low rain and hot summers suit native grapes, with big day-night swings at ripening. They give balanced wines with floral and fruity notes.

styles.text: Whites and reds, young or aged in oak; whites floral and fruity, reds with red fruit and soft tannins.

climate.text: Low rainfall, high summer temperatures and strong day-night temperature swings during ripening.

tastes.text: Whites: pale yellow with green tints; fruity and floral; fresh, balanced, persistent. Reds: cherry red with purple tints; red fruit and flowers; soft tannins. Oak-aged wines add spice and toast.

styles.name: Barrica, Crianza, Reserva, Gran Reserva
styles.text: Oak-aged white or red; spice and toast from the wood.
